summary.text: Monika Johnson-Hostler is a Democratic member of the North Carolina House of Representatives who has represented District 33 since January 2025 and is seeking re-election on November 3, 2026.
She is the executive director of the North Carolina Coalition Against Sexual Assault and previously served on the Wake County school board.

paragraphs.text: Monika Johnson-Hostler is a native of Thomasville, North Carolina.
She received a bachelor's degree in psychology from Fayetteville State University and a master's degree in public administration from North Carolina Central University.

According to Ballotpedia's biography, she has worked for more than 16 years as an advocate for women and children through the North Carolina Coalition Against Sexual Assault, and she lives in Raleigh with her husband and daughter.
Johnson-Hostler represented District 2 on the Wake County Public School System board from 2013 to 2024.
She assumed office in the state House on January 1, 2025, succeeding Rosa Gill.
The Democratic primary for her seat on March 3, 2026, was canceled, and Republican Matthew Orr is her general election opponent.
